original_question: Can a nontrivial well-defined composition of reflections from smooth germs of hypersurfaces ever be equal to the identity, or must every such composition differ from the identity map?
target_in_paper: Alexey Glutsyuk, Problem 2 in arXiv:2110.10750, specifically the unnumbered stronger Ivrii-type conjecture: “no well-defined composition of reflections from smooth germs of hypersurfaces can be equal to the identity.”
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the target statement: it is about compositions of reflections, the local/germ setting for smooth hypersurfaces, the requirement that the composition be well-defined, and the yes/no issue of whether such a composition can ever equal the identity.
missing_details: The ambient setting is Euclidean space R^{n+1}, with arbitrary dimension n ≥ 1 in the cited technical setup.
The reflections act on oriented lines (the local billiard phase space), not directly on points of the hypersurfaces.
The hypersurfaces are C^∞-smooth germs (local hypersurfaces); in the local formulation, no convexity assumption is imposed.
The composition should be explicitly finite and nonempty.
“Well-defined” should be spelled out in pseudogroup/local-map terms: all intermediate reflections and the total composition are defined on a common nonempty open domain of oriented lines.
“Equal to the identity” should mean equality as a local map on that domain/open set, not merely fixing one line or one point.
The operator should be identified as the local billiard reflection in the tangent hyperplane at the transverse intersection point of the oriented line with the hypersurface germ.
The paper-critical exclusion of inverses should be stated: the analogous statement for compositions of reflections together with inverses is explicitly noted to be false.
If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should mention that this is presented as a stronger local version of the usual Ivrii-type non-identity statement for billiard iterates.
refined_question: Let n ≥ 1, and let Σ1, ..., Σm be C^∞-smooth germs of hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}. For each Σj, let T_{Σj} denote the corresponding local billiard-reflection map acting on oriented lines transverse to Σj (reflection in the tangent hyperplane at the intersection point, with the usual billiard reorientation), and suppose that the finite nonempty composition T_{Σm} ∘ ... ∘ T_{Σ1} is well-defined on a nonempty open set of oriented lines. Is it true that such a composition can never coincide with the identity map on that open set?
justification: The draft is not aiming at the approximation/density question in the same Problem 2; it is aiming at the later, sharper Ivrii-type sentence on page 416 of arXiv:2110.10750. That sentence is the nearest official formulation in the paper itself. However, arXiv:2110.10750 is a problem collection and does not itself define the local reflection maps in full detail. The needed stand-alone precision comes from the paper it explicitly cites there, namely [14, §1.6], together with the surrounding setup in [14, §§1.1–1.2]: reflections from hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}, the deformation and compositional-difference notation, the local phase-space/pseudogroup viewpoint, and the local germ framework. The numbered items Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 do not occur in arXiv:2110.10750 itself; the closest faithful target here is the unnumbered stronger Ivrii-type conjecture in Glutsyuk’s Problem 2.
